MSLIV1017-00009.summary: The release of the Infante D. Duarte: the French king's letters to Prince Thomas and Longueville to intercept his escort to Milan, Spanish prisoners of rank to be exchanged for him, force or flight too dangerous for his life, secrecy essential.
MSLIV1017-00009.en:
1. (... with which you were handling and seeking) the release of the Infante Dom Duarte, my most beloved and esteemed brother, (and how you had sought) letters from the Most Christian King by which Prince Thomas and the Duke of Longueville were to intercept the troops escorting the Infante to Milan, (and how you also sought to be given) some Spanish prisoners of the Most Christian King, persons of rank, so as to obtain the Infante's freedom in exchange for them.
2. ... such as those of exchange or escape, rather than[?] those of force, like the ones you intended to attempt with the Most Christian King's letters, would be very dangerous for the Infante's life, since it is reported that those who moved him from Germany to Milan carried orders to kill him should anyone try to take him on the road;

MSLIV1017-00013.summary: French ships licensed for Madagascar; Richelieu reported dead, the man who most fomented the war with Castile; Nisa to penetrate the secrets of Castile and of the French court.
MSLIV1017-00013.en:
A. (... and of the licence) that the Most Christian King was granting to his vassal Rigão and others to send their ships and men to the island of São Lourenço [Madagascar], open trade and build forts.
B. (... although the news is not certain) you [..] most fomented the wars and discords with Castile, and that on his account the offers made of a settlement and cessation of arms were often not admitted; and that if the Cardinal's death should prove true, it is to be feared
C. that Castile may pursue the same approaches and have better success; (wherefore I charge and command you) above all the other matters in your charge to try, with the caution and secrecy that are needed, to penetrate the secrets of Castile and the mind of the Most Christian King and his ministers, so as to warn me of it.
D. [..] (legible only in part; the clear copy gives the text:

MSLIV1017-00153.summary: The marriages of Prince Teodósio and the Infantas are not to be confided to the marquês de Cascais or anyone else.
MSLIV1017-00153.en: ... since it does not extend to the marriages of the Prince, my son beloved above all, and of the Infantas, about which I had you written: for you shall neither tell nor entrust these to the Marquis [de Cascais] nor to any other[?] person, except [..] ordered [..].

system: Two letter-for-letter substitution alphabets with a few homophones, written as pseudo-words with word divisions kept, plus a symbol for Castile and a code word for the French king: alphabet A in Latin letters (1642-43), alphabet B in Greek-shaped signs…
